issue.title: Test Gap: [dualtor] test to cover tunnel term drop scenario

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the test gap

To avoid traffic looping between the two ToRs when they are both in standby.

Traffic loss is less of a concern but the congestion.

### Affected Area

Active-Active dualtor. Active-standby dualtor.

### Impact of missing tests and proposed tests

Test to verify tunnel termination drops.

resolution.title: [dualtor] Add test for tunnel termination drop on standby ToR
resolution.description:
### Description of PR
Summary:

The test injects the receiving side of the loop-prevention scenario described in issue https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/issues/21092: a standby ToR receives an IPinIP packet, and verifies the receiving ToR drops it instead of forwarding or re-encapsulating it.

Fixes #21092

### Type of change
- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [x] New Test case
    - [ ] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [ ] Test case improvement

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
Issue #21092 identifies a test gap: there is no test to verify tunnel termination drop behavior for the loop-prevention path. If both ToRs are in standby, one standby ToR can tunnel traffic to the peer. The peer standby ToR must drop the terminated tunnel packet; otherwise traffic can be re-encapsulated and loop between ToRs.

#### How did you do it?
Added `tests/dualtor/test_tunnel_term_drop.py` with `test_tunnel_term_drop_standby`:

1. Put the selected ToR into standby mode.
2. Build an IPinIP packet as if sent from the peer ToR:
   - outer src = peer ToR loopback
   - outer dst = local ToR loopback
   - inner dst = server IP
3. Test sequence inside the test body:
   a. `sonic-clear counters` on the standby DUT
   b. `ptfadapter.dataplane.flush()`
   c. `testutils.send(count=1000)` from a T1 PTF port
   d. `verify_no_packet` — confirms the packet is NOT decapsulated and forwarded to the server port
   e. `tunnel_traffic_monitor(..., existing=False)` — confirms it is NOT re-encapsulated back toward T1
   f. Port counters are logged for debug only (no assertion), per review feedback.

For active-active dualtor, it moves only the selected mux port to standby before the same drop verification runs. This covers both cable types (active-standby and active-active) as called out in issue #21092.

#### How did you verify/test it?
Cisco 8101C01 libra: https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6a2bba2195ed954f0d3d7aef
Cisco 8101C01 gemini: https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6a2bb9eb03b7f75ed1c22bca
Arista-7260 libra:
Arista 7050 gemini:

#### Any platform specific information?
No platform-specific requirements. Uses standard dualtor IPinIP tunnel infrastructure.
